newsitem.title: USA: Iowa Gov says county should sell profitable track.
newsitem.headline: Iowa Gov says county should sell profitable track.

text.p: Iowa Gov. Terry Branstad believes Polk County supervisors should sell their highly profitable race track and casino to aid local schools.
Branstad said Monday he believes Polk County cannot continue running the Prairie Meadows Race Track, which it came to own by underwriting bonds for the facility during hard times.
Since the installation of slot machines the track has become profitable and the bonds have been paid off, making this an appropriate time to get out of the business, Branstad said.
"The law clearly requires that racing facilities be operated by non-profit corporations and Polk County is not a non-profit corporation," Branstad said.
Polk County supervisors are considering selling Prairie Meadows to a private developer and have been negotiating a lease agreement for the facility with the Racing Association of Central Iowa.

"I have thought that for a long time that the county should sell it,' Branstad said. "The county only owned it because they basically got stuck with it and now that the bonds have been paid off it seems to me that it would be in the interest of the taxpayers."
Proceeds from a sale could finance repairs for most of the schools in Polk County, Branstad said.
The facility was appraised at $160 million in May. Polk County received a $200 million unsolicited offer for the track shortly after its appraised value was announced.
An economic impact study released earlier this month suggested the track would be worth as much as $294 million to a private operator which would likely more than double the number of slot machines.
Polk County projects a $16.8 million fiscal 1998 profit from the facility, which supervisors have voted to share with public schools and use for human services needs.
